newsitem.title: USA: NBC wins Nielsen TV ratings for March 17 week.
newsitem.headline: NBC wins Nielsen TV ratings for March 17 week.

text.p: NBC continues to control prime time television viewer ratings, leading for the week of March 17 to March 23 based on the strength of its Thursday night lineup, Nielsen Media Research said Tuesday.
NBC, a unit of General Electric Co, posted 9.3 rating points with a 16 percent share.
NBC's "Seinfeld" won first place for the week, followed by "Friends", "Suddenly Susan" and "Naked Truth." Those are all programs shown Thursday nights.
The long-running "60 Minutes" Sunday night news show on CBS, a unit of Westinghouse Electric Corp, came in fifth for the week, followed by NBC's "Law and Order."
The ratings points represent a percentage of homes with televisions and the share represents the percentage of television sets turned in at a particular time.

Nielsen, a unit of Cognizant Corp, said CBS posted 8.9 rating points with a 15 percent share. ABC, which is owned by Walt Disney Co, posted 9.0 rating points with a 15 percent share. A rating of 6.7 points put News Corp's Fox in fourth place. Viacom Inc's UPN and Time Warner Inc's WB networks posted ratings of 3.4 and 2.6, respectively.
